The speaker deliberately killed someone as part of a crime. Afterward, they wrote the same sentence repeatedly to practice imitating the victim’s handwriting. They intend to forge a note in the victim’s hand, addressed to someone else, making it appear that the victim has left and will not return. The note is meant to support a cover story for the killing, but the speaker is struggling to make the handwriting convincing and fears that the forgery—and therefore the crime—may be exposed.

They plan to send a forged handwritten note, supposedly from the victim, telling its recipient that the victim is disappointed in them and has left voluntarily. The speaker also plans to send later communications while pretending to be the victim, as part of a fraud designed to make people believe the victim is still alive and postpone discovery of the death—not to obtain money or property.
